text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-82471 fired to #incidents and @eng-oncall — multiple GPU hosts reporting kernel crash followed by kubelet NotReady. Affected hosts: gpu-rack-18-node07, gpu-rack-18-node08, gpu-rack-19-node02. Severity: P1. Auto-escalation in 5m if not acked. Link: https://pd.example/pd/PD-82471

alex: ack — I'm oncall. grabbing serial consoles and checking node states.

maya: I see node states in k8s API: two nodes NotReady, one Flake. Some customer-facing pods on those nodes show CrashLoopBackOff and Evicted.

sam: paste of `kubectl get nodes -o wide` output I pulled:
```
NAME                    STATUS     ROLES   AGE   VERSION
gpu-rack-18-node07      NotReady   <none>  120d  v1.27.3
gpu-rack-18-node08      NotReady   <none>  98d   v1.27.3
gpu-rack-19-node02      Ready      <none>  60d   v1.27.3
```

ryan: from serial console on node07 I see kernel oops followed by GPU driver stacktrace, then watchdog reset. snippet:
```
[ 3234.512345] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 3234.512349] Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
```

natalie: node08 logs show kubelet losing heartbeat after kernel messages. systemd-journal has `oom-killer` entries but root cause looks like PCI reset + driver crash.

alex: status check: customer impact? maya — any 5xx surge in edge logs?

maya: yes — ingress shows spike in 502 for model-serving cluster in us-west-2 around the same time (~1.5% of QPS for the endpoint). Most retries succeeded on fallback nodes but latency bump visible. customer-impact: partial, degraded for small subset of requests.

sam: i'm going to cordon and drain the surviving GPU nodes in rack-18 to stop further churn. plan: cordon node07/08 (if reachable), drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for urgent evacs.

alex: try soft-drain first, don't force-delete long-lived stateful pods until we confirm replicas. use `kubectl drain node07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`

ryan: i'm attaching ILR (serial) to node07 and requesting HW out-of-band: IPMI shows no POST after panic. opening RMA ticket with datacenter, tags: gpu-fault, pci-reset.

natalie: quick mitigation — spinning up two replacement `gpu-ephemeral` instances in us-west-2 (Dedicated pool) to soak traffic while we evacuate. I'll bump autoscaler min by +2 on that pool.

alex: good. maya — please add customers page note minimal impact and that we're working on hardware-level RMA + draining. include timeframe and keep updates every 15m.

maya: noted. drafting update: "We're investigating a host-level failure in us-west-2 affecting a small subset of ML inference requests. We're draining impacted hosts and provisioning replacement capacity; most traffic is routing to healthy nodes. ETA for mitigation ~30-60m." posting to status page now.

sam: drain commands run on node07 but kubelet isn't responding on node08 — cordon succeeded on node07 only. running `kubectl get pods -n model-serving -o wide | grep node07` to verify evac.

alex: if kubelet hangs, use `kubectl delete node` as last resort after confirm pods rescheduled. before that, add node-level annotation to prevent scheduling and notify downstream schedulers.

ryan: datacenter responded — physical host on rack-18 shows GPU PCIe error counters high, power-cycling under RMA is allowed. they'll attempt power-cycle now.

natalie: replacement GPUs coming up in pool; autoscaler shows new nodes registering: gpu-dyn-23 and gpu-dyn-24. Routing shows reduced error rate already, 502s down to 0.3% of QPS.

maria (oncall-bot): reminder to follow handoff checklist if this goes beyond 2 hours: escalate to SRE lead, open incident doc, collect kernel+serial dumps.

alex: logging action items to incident doc, assigning followups: ryan->RMA coord, sam->drain/evac and pod reschedule verification, natalie->capacity bump and telemetry, maya->customer comms and status page.

sam: evacuated node07 pods successfully, most replicas on gpu-dyn-23/24. A couple of stateful pods delayed due to PVC binding — working with storage to force-provision.

ryan: RMA update: power-cycle completed, node08 came back briefly then hit driver panic again, so engineering agreed to isolate host. datacenter will pull card for diagnostics.

alex: ok — isolate affected hosts from scheduler (already cordoned). proceed with RMA and hardware diag. keeping PD incident open until all nodes stable and customer impact cleared. next update in 15m or sooner if things change.

maya: status update posted to customers; ops Slack thread pinned to incident doc.

natalie: metrics look healthy after replacements warmed up, latency back to baseline for 95/99. small error tail persists but trending down.

alex: handing off to evening oncall @ryan in 30m — if you accept, give a quick rundown and confirm watch.

ryan: I accept. I have RMA ticket, node isolation, and followups. Will monitor PD alert channel and escalate to SRE lead if regression >0.5% 5xx or if further host panics observed.

alex: thanks — closing loop here. incident status: mitigated (traffic routed to replacements), root cause under hardware investigation (GPU PCIe/driver failure). incident doc link: https://incidents.example/INC-2024-231

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged and handed off to ryan.
